question: Got caught with weed at 18 and was convicted. Is my Pell gone for good?
reference_answer: No. A drug conviction no longer affects eligibility for federal student aid. The FAFSA Simplification Act removed the rule, the FAFSA no longer asks the question, and schools can't use it to deny federal aid.

sources.title: Early Implementation of the FAFSA Simplification Act's Removal of Selective Service and Drug Conviction Requirements (Federal Register)

question: Counselor here: do male students still have to register for Selective Service before they can get federal aid?
must_not_include: required to register to get aid
reference_answer: No. The FAFSA Simplification Act removed Selective Service registration as a requirement for federal student aid, and the FAFSA no longer asks about it. Registration is a separate obligation, but it isn't tied to aid eligibility.

sources.title: Early Implementation of the FAFSA Simplification Act's Removal of Selective Service and Drug Conviction Requirements (Federal Register)

question: I have DACA and a social security number. Since I have an SSN, can I get Pell and federal loans?
must_not_include: DACA recipients are eligible for federal
reference_answer: No. Having an SSN through DACA doesn't make you eligible for federal student aid; deferred action isn't an eligible noncitizen status. You may still be able to get state, college or private aid, and some states and schools use the FAFSA for that, so check with your state agency and the school's aid office.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 1, Ch. 2: U.S. Citizenship & Eligible Noncitizens
2026-27 FSA Handbook, Application and Verification Guide, Ch. 2: Filling Out the FAFSA Form

question: Parent asking: I'm undocumented but my daughter is a citizen. Will my status make her ineligible for aid?
reference_answer: No. A parent's immigration status isn't considered in determining a student's eligibility for federal student aid. Your daughter can qualify if she meets the requirements. Your status matters only if you wanted a Parent PLUS loan or federal aid for your own studies.

question: My brother is serving time in a state prison. Is there any federal money for him to take college classes?
reference_answer: Yes, a Pell Grant may be available if he enrolls in an eligible prison education program run by a participating school. Incarcerated students can't get Direct Loans while incarcerated, and the school running the program decides eligibility.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 1, Ch. 1: School-Determined Requirements
sources.section: Confined or incarcerated individuals and prison education programs

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 7, Ch. 1: Student Eligibility for Pell Grants

question: My high school gave me a certificate of completion instead of a diploma. Does that work for the FAFSA?
reference_answer: A certificate of attendance or completion on its own isn't enough for federal aid. You need a diploma or recognized equivalent such as a GED or HiSET, completed homeschooling under state law, or to qualify through the ability-to-benefit rules, for example in an eligible career pathway program.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 1, Ch. 1: School-Determined Requirements

question: No diploma or GED, first time in college. What are the ability-to-benefit options?
reference_answer: For a new student, ability to benefit works only in an eligible career pathway program. You then also pass an approved test, complete six credit hours or 225 clock hours toward a degree or certificate, or complete an approved state process.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 1, Ch. 1: School-Determined Requirements

question: Taking just one 3-credit class this term. What federal aid can I still get?
must_not_include: you can still get Direct Loans
reference_answer: Pell Grants don't require half-time enrollment, so you may get a prorated Pell. Direct Loans require at least half-time enrollment, so at one class you generally can't get them. Your school sets enrollment status for your program.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 1, Ch. 1: School-Determined Requirements

question: I defaulted on a federal loan. Is there any way to get eligible for aid again without paying the whole thing?
must_not_include: you can never get aid again
reference_answer: Yes. You can consolidate the defaulted loan, make six consecutive full, voluntary, on-time payments under a repayment arrangement (a one-time option), or rehabilitate the loan with nine on-time payments within 10 months. Contact your loan holder to start.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 1, Ch. 3: NSLDS Financial Aid History

question: I have a BA in history and I'm enrolling in a BSN nursing program. Pell or no Pell?
must_not_include: you can get Pell for a second bachelor's
you are eligible for Pell again
reference_answer: Generally no Pell. Students who completed a bachelor's degree are ineligible for Pell even for a second bachelor's. The exceptions are certain post-baccalaureate teacher certification programs and, starting July 1, 2026, eligible workforce programs. Loans may still be available.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 7, Ch. 1: Student Eligibility for Pell Grants

question: Entered foster care at 15, got adopted at 16. Am I dependent on my adoptive parents for the FAFSA?
reference_answer: No, you're independent. A student who was in foster care or a ward of the court at any time since age 13 is independent even if their status changed later. The school may ask for documentation.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Application and Verification Guide, Ch. 2: Filling Out the FAFSA Form
sources.section: Orphan, ward of the court, or foster care

question: I'm at the Naval Academy. Do I check the veteran box?
reference_answer: No. Students attending a U.S. military academy or in ROTC aren't veterans for FAFSA purposes. A veteran generally served on active duty for other than training and was discharged other than dishonorably.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Application and Verification Guide, Ch. 2: Filling Out the FAFSA Form

question: Spending spring at a university in Spain through my college. Can I keep my federal loans and Pell?
reference_answer: Usually yes. You can keep federal aid while studying abroad if you stay enrolled as a regular student at your home school and the home school approves the program for academic credit. Check with your study abroad and financial aid offices.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 2, Ch. 2: Program Eligibility, Written Arrangements, and Distance Education

question: I'm 19 and living in a shelter. What proof does a college accept that I'm an unaccompanied homeless youth?
reference_answer: A determination from a school district homeless liaison, a shelter or homeless youth program director, or a TRIO or GEAR UP director is accepted. Without one, the aid administrator decides from a written statement or documented interview. Police reports aren't required, and the reason you're homeless isn't the focus.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Application and Verification Guide, Ch. 2: Filling Out the FAFSA Form
2026-27 FSA Handbook, Application and Verification Guide, Ch. 5: Special Cases

question: Can you guarantee my school will approve me as independent if I have a pending dependency override?
reference_answer: No one can guarantee it. A financial aid administrator decides overrides case by case based on documentation of unusual circumstances like abandonment, abuse or incarceration. Parents refusing to help or not claiming you on taxes doesn't qualify. Send the documents the aid office asks for quickly.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Application and Verification Guide, Ch. 5: Special Cases
